status: Native source checks passed; not yet published or deployed

reproduction.runtime: Native Alchemy workerd service binding and actual local R2
reproduction.scope: Initial fixture failed before glob import. The fixture was subsequently extended with cache replacement and request-budget cases.

change: Native Rust os.scandir, DirEntry and ScandirIterator use the existing authorized filesystem.readdir/stat operations; no new filesystem transport or persistence owner.
Name, inode and non-symlink type checks use the captured directory listing, without a per-entry stat request. Native iterators support close, context manager cleanup and exhaustion.
Names and paths retain str/UTF-8 bytes mode, original relative path spelling and __fspath__ support. Positive descriptor input explicitly rejects unsupported directory-fd enumeration.

Stat caches are separate when following an enumerated symlink; enumerated non-symlinks share lstat metadata for follow modes, including namespace replacement by a symlink. Errors are preserved; dangling type checks return false on ENOENT.
Pinned standard-library glob and fnmatch are frozen unchanged; os.curdir references the pinned posixpath constant.
coverage: str, UTF-8 bytes and path-like directory inputs; keyword, omitted and None paths; relative path identity; native entry/iterator construction denied.
File, directory, symlink, directory symlink, dangling target and loop metadata; inode identity; follow/no-follow and cache identity; stale metadata after write and non-symlink replacement.
Explicit/double close, exhaustion, context exit after exception, read-only metadata and unfinished iteration.
Closed original Worker followed by another native Worker over the same R2: cached entries, a partial native iterator, lazy glob generator, cwd and pinned module globals persist.

Current capability denies readless enumeration and readonly writes; current directory modes deny enumeration and uncached stat. Previously admitted cached metadata remains guest data. A foreign sandbox file is excluded.
Glob patterns, hidden files, recursive traversal, root_dir, bytes and iglob; fnmatch matching and case behavior.

512 distinct regular entries are classified with inode/is_file/is_dir/is_symlink under the unchanged 256 host-request ceiling. This proves bounded host access for this workload, not a latency or billing measurement.
development: First native integration reached glob and exposed missing os.curdir; it now reuses posixpath.curdir.
A test fixture included unsupported chmod.follow; the actual chmod contract was restored before the successful native run.

A CPython namespace-replacement probe showed that an enumerated non-symlink uses shared lstat metadata even after replacement by a symlink. The final implementation and native regression preserve that behavior.
limits: Directory descriptors, resource warnings, full pathlib, complete errno/POSIX and full stdlib/pip remain open.
Directory entries use a bounded eager snapshot from the existing filesystem listing. Mutation visibility during enumeration is unspecified; cached attributes are intentionally stale.
Stock glob suppression of OSError is unchanged; unsupported directory-fd operations do not become supported through glob.
No new production, maximum-scale memory, comparative latency, CPU, billing or AgentOS cost claim.
This changes the Python binary and requires explicit reset of existing Python contexts on adoption. Published/deployed 0.28.0 is unchanged.
